records.source: חָ֭כְמוֹת בָּנְתָ֣ה בֵיתָ֑הּ חָצְבָ֖ה עַמּוּדֶ֣יהָ שִׁבְעָֽה׃
records.gloss: Wisdom has built her house; she has hewn her pillars, seven.
pieces: Wisdom has built a house for herself \q and shaped seven pillars for it.

L.1: Wisdom has built her house; \q she has hewn her pillars, seven [of them].

R.1: Wisdom has a new house. \q She has made seven strong columns to hold it up.

decisions.choice: Wisdom: the plural form of 1:20
decisions.reason: The same plural of fullness (hokmot) as in 1:20.

decisions.choice: seven pillars: a large, complete house
decisions.reason: Seven is the number of completeness. A house with seven pillars is a grand house, fit for a feast. Many meanings have been suggested; the text does not say.

records.heading: Wisdom's feast

records.source: טָבְחָ֣ה טִ֭בְחָהּ מָסְכָ֣ה יֵינָ֑הּ אַ֝֗ף עָֽרְכָ֥ה שֻׁלְחָנָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: She has slaughtered her slaughter; she has mixed her wine; also she has set her table.
pieces: She has slaughtered her animals for the feast, mixed her wine \q and set her table.

L.2: She has slaughtered her meat; she has mixed her wine; \q she has also set her table.

R.2: She has cooked meat, mixed wine and set the table for a big meal.

decisions.choice: mixed her wine: with spices or water
decisions.reason: Wine was mixed with spices for a feast (Song of Songs 8:2) or with water. The feast is ready; only guests are needed.

decisions.choice: slaughtered her meat: set against the woman of 7:14
decisions.reason: The strange woman also had meat from her offerings (7:14). Two feasts are offered in this chapter.

records.source: שָֽׁלְחָ֣ה נַעֲרֹתֶ֣יהָ תִקְרָ֑א עַל־גַּ֝פֵּ֗י מְרֹ֣מֵי קָֽרֶת׃
records.gloss: She has sent out her maidservants; she calls on [the] tops of [the] heights of [the] town:
pieces: She has sent her young women out with the invitation; \q she calls from the high places of the town:

L.3: She has sent out her young women; \q she calls from the highest points of the town:

R.3: She has sent her servant girls to invite people. \q She calls out from the highest places in the town:

decisions.choice: her young women: servants who carry the invitation
decisions.reason: A host sent servants to call the guests (Matthew 22:3).

records.source: מִי־פֶ֭תִי יָסֻ֣ר הֵ֑נָּה חֲסַר־לֵ֝֗ב אָ֣מְרָה לּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Who [is] simple, let him turn in here; [one] lacking heart, she says to him:
pieces: "Whoever is naive, come in here!" \q To anyone who lacks sense she says,

L.4: "Whoever [is] simple, let {{gender:them|him}} turn in here!" \q To one lacking heart she says,

R.4: "If you do not know much about life, come in here!" \q To people who do not have good sense she says,

decisions.choice: whoever is simple, turn in here: repeated by Folly in 9:16
decisions.reason: Folly uses Wisdom's very words in verse 16. The simple must choose between two invitations that sound alike.

records.source: לְ֭כוּ לַחֲמ֣וּ בְֽלַחֲמִ֑י וּ֝שְׁת֗וּ בְּיַ֣יִן מָסָֽכְתִּי׃
records.gloss: Come, eat of my bread, and drink of [the] wine I have mixed.
pieces: "Come, have some of my food \q and taste the wine I have blended.

L.5: "Come, eat of my bread, \q and drink of [the] wine I have mixed.

R.5: "Come and eat my food. \q Drink the wine I have made.

decisions.choice: eat ... drink: Wisdom's teaching as food
decisions.reason: The meal stands for the teaching Wisdom gives (Isaiah 55:1–3). Jesus too spoke of himself as bread (John 6:35).

records.source: עִזְב֣וּ פְתָאיִ֣ם וִֽחְי֑וּ וְ֝אִשְׁר֗וּ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ בִּינָֽה׃
records.gloss: Abandon simpleness and live, and walk straight in [the] way of understanding.
pieces: Leave your naive ways behind and live; \q walk straight down the road of understanding.

L.6: Leave [your] simpleness and live, \q and walk straight in [the] way of understanding.

R.6: Stop being foolish, and you will live. \q Learn to understand.

decisions.choice: simpleness: the ways of the simple, or the simple people themselves
decisions.reason: The word (petayim) is the plural used for "simple ones". It may mean "leave the simple", their company, or "leave simpleness".

decisions.choice: walk straight: the verb of 4:14
decisions.reason: The verb (ashar) shares its root with "how blessed".

records.source: יֹ֤סֵ֨ר׀לֵ֗ץ לֹקֵ֣חַֽ ל֣וֹ קָל֑וֹן וּמוֹכִ֖יחַ לְרָשָׁ֣ע מוּמֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: [One] correcting a mocker receives for himself dishonor, and [one] reproving a wicked [person], his blemish.
pieces: Correct a mocker and you will be insulted; \q rebuke the wicked and you will get hurt.

L.7: Whoever corrects a mocker gets dishonor for {{gender:themselves|himself}}, \q and whoever reproves a wicked [person gets] {{gender:their|his}} [own] blemish.

R.7: If you correct people who make fun of others, they will insult you. \q If you correct evil people, they will hurt you.

decisions.choice: verses 7–12: Wisdom's sayings about who can be taught
decisions.reason: The section is a set of sayings set between the two invitations. Verse 11 ("by me") shows Wisdom is still speaking.

decisions.choice: his blemish: abuse, a hurt
decisions.reason: The word (mum) is a blemish or injury. The one who rebukes the wicked comes away hurt or insulted.

records.source: אַל־תּ֣וֹכַח לֵ֭ץ פֶּן־יִשְׂנָאֶ֑ךָּ הוֹכַ֥ח לְ֝חָכָ֗ם וְיֶאֱהָבֶֽךָּ׃
records.gloss: Do not reprove a mocker, lest he hate you; reprove a wise [person], and he will love you.
pieces: Do not rebuke a mocker, or you will be hated; \q rebuke the wise, and you will be loved.

L.8: Do not reprove a mocker, lest {{gender:they|he}} hate you; \q reprove a wise [person], and {{gender:they|he}} will love you.

R.8: Do not correct people who make fun of others, or they will hate you. \q Correct wise people, and they will love you.

decisions.choice: a mocker: one who scorns correction
decisions.reason: The mocker (lets) of 1:22: he cannot be taught because he will not be corrected (13:1; 15:12).

records.source: תֵּ֣ן לְ֭חָכָם וְיֶחְכַּם־ע֑וֹד הוֹדַ֥ע לְ֝צַדִּ֗יק וְי֣וֹסֶף לֶֽקַח׃פ
records.gloss: Give to a wise [person], and he will become wiser still; teach a righteous [person], and he will increase learning.
pieces: Give advice to the wise and they will grow wiser still; \q teach the righteous and they will add to what they know.

L.9: Give to a wise [person], and {{gender:they|he}} will be wiser still; \q teach a righteous [person], and {{gender:they|he}} will increase in learning.

R.9: Teach wise people, and they will become even wiser. \q Teach good people, and they will learn more.

decisions.choice: increase in learning: as in 1:5
decisions.reason: The book's opening promise (1:5) applies to those who are already wise.

records.source: תְּחִלַּ֣ת חָ֭כְמָה יִרְאַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה וְדַ֖עַת קְדֹשִׁ֣ים בִּינָֽה׃
records.gloss: [The] beginning of wisdom [is the] fear of YHWH, and [the] knowledge of [the] Holy One [is] understanding.
pieces: Wisdom starts with the fear of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and to know the Holy One is understanding.

L.10: [The] beginning of wisdom [is the] fear of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and [the] knowledge of [the] Holy One [is] understanding.

R.10: Becoming wise begins with honoring {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with awe. \q Knowing the holy God is what it means to understand.

decisions.choice: the beginning of wisdom is the fear of the LORD: as in 1:7
decisions.reason: Chapters 1–9 begin and end with this saying. Here the word for beginning (tehillah) means only the starting point.

decisions.choice: the Holy One: a plural of majesty
decisions.reason: The word (qedoshim) is plural, but like the word for God (elohim) it names the one holy God (30:3; Hosea 11:12).

records.heading: Wisdom and the woman Folly

records.source: כִּי־בִ֭י יִרְבּ֣וּ יָמֶ֑יךָ וְיוֹסִ֥יפוּ לְּ֝ךָ֗ שְׁנ֣וֹת חַיִּֽים׃
records.gloss: For by me your days will increase, and they will add to you years of life.
pieces: For through me your days will be many, \q and the years of your life will grow.

L.11: For by me your days will be many, \q and years of life will be added to you.

R.11: If you follow me, you will live a long life.

decisions.choice: by me: Wisdom speaks
decisions.reason: The "me" shows that verses 7–12 are part of Wisdom's speech. The promise is that of 3:2 and 4:10.

records.gloss: If you are wise, you are wise for yourself; and [if] you mock, you alone will bear [it].
pieces: If you are wise, your wisdom will benefit you; \q if you mock, the cost is yours alone."

L.12: If you are wise, you are wise for yourself; \q and [if] you mock, you alone will bear [it]."

R.12: If you are wise, you are the one who will gain. \q If you make fun of wisdom, you are the one who will suffer."

decisions.choice: for yourself ... you alone: each one bears the result
decisions.reason: Wisdom's call is personal: the gain and the loss fall on the one who chooses.

decisions.choice: the verse ends here, as the Hebrew text has it
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation adds several lines after this verse. They are not in the Hebrew text.

records.source: אֵ֣שֶׁת כְּ֭סִילוּת הֹֽמִיָּ֑ה פְּ֝תַיּ֗וּת וּבַל־יָ֥דְעָה מָּֽה׃
records.gloss: A woman of folly [is] loud; [she is] simpleness and does not know anything.
pieces: The woman Folly makes a lot of noise; \q she is gullible and has no knowledge.

L.13: The woman Folly [is] loud; \q [she is] simpleness, and she does not know anything.

R.13: Folly is like a woman who talks too loudly. \q She is foolish and knows nothing.

decisions.choice: the woman Folly: folly pictured as a woman
decisions.reason: As Wisdom is a woman with a house and a feast, so Folly is pictured as her rival. She is loud like the woman of 7:11.

decisions.choice: simpleness: the folly of the simple
decisions.reason: She is not only foolish herself; she is what the simple are.

records.source: וְֽ֭יָשְׁבָה לְפֶ֣תַח בֵּיתָ֑הּ עַל־כִּ֝סֵּ֗א מְרֹ֣מֵי קָֽרֶת׃
records.gloss: And she sits at [the] door of her house, on a seat [at the] heights of [the] town,
pieces: She takes her seat in her doorway, \q on a chair up on the town's heights,

L.14: And she sits at [the] door of her house, \q on a seat [at the] heights of [the] town,

R.14: She sits in her doorway \q or on a chair in the highest place in town,

decisions.choice: the heights of the town: where Wisdom called (9:3)
decisions.reason: Folly copies Wisdom's place and words, but she sits and does not prepare anything.

records.gloss: to call to those passing [on the] road, those going straight [on] their paths:
pieces: calling to those who pass by, \q who are going straight along on their way:

L.15: to call to those who pass by [on the] road, \q who are going straight [on] their paths:

R.15: calling to people who walk by, \q who are minding their own business:

decisions.choice: going straight: people not looking for her
decisions.reason: Her targets are people on their way somewhere else. She draws them off their straight path.

records.source: מִי־פֶ֭תִי יָסֻ֣ר הֵ֑נָּה וַחֲסַר־לֵ֝֗ב וְאָ֣מְרָה לּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Who [is] simple, let him turn in here; and [one] lacking heart, she says to him:
pieces: "Whoever is naive, come in here!" \q And to anyone who lacks sense she says,

L.16: "Whoever [is] simple, let {{gender:them|him}} turn in here!" \q And to one lacking heart she says,

R.16: "If you do not know much about life, come in here!" \q To people who do not have good sense she says,

decisions.choice: the same words as Wisdom's (9:4)
decisions.reason: Folly's call is word for word the same as Wisdom's. The difference is in what each offers.

records.gloss: Stolen waters are sweet, and bread of secrecy is pleasant.
pieces: "Water that is stolen tastes sweet, \q and food eaten where no one sees is a delight."

L.17: "Stolen waters are sweet, \q and bread [eaten] in secret is pleasant."

R.17: "Water you steal tastes sweeter. \q Food you eat in secret tastes better."

decisions.choice: stolen waters: forbidden love
decisions.reason: Water stands for married love in 5:15–18. Folly offers what belongs to someone else, and its sweetness comes from its being forbidden.

decisions.choice: bread: Folly has no feast of her own
decisions.reason: Wisdom prepared meat and wine (9:2); Folly offers only stolen water and bread.

records.source: וְֽלֹא־יָ֭דַע כִּֽי־רְפָאִ֣ים שָׁ֑ם בְּעִמְקֵ֖י שְׁא֣וֹל קְרֻאֶֽיהָ׃פ
records.gloss: And he does not know that [the] shades [are] there; in [the] depths of Sheol [are] her invited ones.
pieces: But those who turn in have no idea that the dead are in that house, \q that her guests lie deep in Sheol.

L.18: But {{gender:they do|he does}} not know that [the] shades [are] there, \q [that] her guests [are] in [the] depths of Sheol.

R.18: But people who go into her house do not know that it is full of dead people. \q Everyone she invites ends up in the grave.

decisions.choice: the shades: the dead
decisions.reason: The word (rephaim) of 2:18.

decisions.choice: the chapter ends here, as the Hebrew text has it
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation adds lines after this verse urging the reader to flee and drink from his own well. They are not in the Hebrew text.

decisions.choice: they
decisions.reason: Balanced uses "they" for the one who turns in, whom verse 16 does not limit to men.
